concept: Scrubber is the position of a track or a video on a dial player, a frosted glass cap riding the fader groove like the tape position on a deck, the played stretch lit in its quiet tint, with chapter marks printed above, the buffered stretch drawn as a thin ink line along the groove floor and the elapsed and remaining time printed in tabular figures under its ends, while the orange stays on the play key.

material.recipe: A frosted tinted resin, lit from behind by the value

default_to_avoid.pattern: YouTube style scrubber: a red progress bar that fills as it plays with a round scrubber dot
default_to_avoid.why_not: A red fill spends the accent and the hue of a fault on a reading, while P1 keeps the one loud part for the play key and P3 asks for a cap in a groove.

default_to_avoid.pattern: scrubber that only shows time on hover in a floating bubble
default_to_avoid.why_not: P2 says the state must be readable at a glance, so the elapsed and remaining time are printed all the time and never hidden behind a pointer.

references.source: Braun TG 1000 tape recorder (Dieter Rams, 1970): a tape counter and a linear position scale on the deck
Braun audio 1 compact system (Dieter Rams, 1962): linear faders in a slot with a printed ruler scale
packages/react/src/components/Slider (dial): the cap and groove of the ruler fader

derivation.consequence: faders ride a groove with a ruler scale
derivation.form: The cap rides Slider's narrow recessed groove, and the ruler above it prints only the chapter starts as ink marks.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The groove and the buffered stretch are plastic and ink and the cap is quiet glass, so the transport's play key stays the one orange part.

derivation.consequence: a glass part is lit through from behind by the value it holds, and keeps the one top-left light on its surface
derivation.form: The played stretch of the groove is lit in the cap's tint, the frosted cap shows that light through itself and keeps the lit hairline and short shadow.

derivation.consequence: glass appears on caps, lamps, latched keys and chips only, never on a body, panel or card
derivation.form: Only the cap is glass; the groove, the chapter marks, the times and the player card around it stay matte plastic and printing.

derivation.consequence: holes are ink at a lower step
derivation.form: The buffered stretch is a 2px line in line.ring along the middle of the groove floor, a lower ink step and never a played fill.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: Elapsed time prints under the start of the groove and remaining time under its end, in tabular figures so they never jitter.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: The track is a role slider whose value text reads 1:23 of 3:45: arrows move 5 seconds, PageUp and PageDown 30, Home and End the ends.
While playing the cap steps with the time and does not spring; only a seek by key or by hand travels on the spring.

options.name: tape fader: Slider's cap and groove, chapter marks above, buffered line, times under the ends
counter window: an LCD tape counter above a hairline groove with a needle
inline transport: elapsed and remaining on the groove's own line

variants.reason: A reuses the fader every dial person already knows and keeps the groove its full length whatever the times say (P6); B adds a second display window that P2 keeps to one and a needle too thin to grab, and C shortens the groove as the times grow.

mechanism.travel: full track length, one second per position

root.why: The scrubber fills the inline size of its column and keeps at least five touch targets of length in every state.

header.why: The name of what is playing is printed on the line above the track, at its start, like the label above a fader.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, the same printing as every fader label on the case.

fader.why: The whole track is the hit area and stays at least 44px tall although the groove itself draws narrower.

chapters.why: The band above the groove is the ruler, and it prints a mark only where a chapter starts, spanning the cap's travel.

chapter.why: Each chapter mark is printing in the primary ink at the ring stroke, flat on the material with no shadow.

groove.why: The cap rides the narrow recessed slot drawn with inverse light; its hairline edge in line.ring holds 3:1 against the body.

buffer.why: The stretch that has loaded is a thin line of lower step ink along the groove floor, visible in both themes and never orange.

cap.why: The cap is a raised part of frosted glass in the track's tint, showing the played light through itself and casting the short part shadow down and to the right of the single light.

fill.why: The played stretch is lit in the cap's quiet tint up to the cap's centre, so the position reads as light behind glass and never as the orange.

times.why: Elapsed and remaining time are printed under the two ends of the groove, on one line that never moves the track.

time.why: Each time is set in tabular figures at the smallest size step, so the digits keep their width as the track plays.

hover.why: Hover darkens the cap's printed index one step and never lifts or grows the cap toward the pointer.

focus-visible.why: Focus is the system ring in secondary printing ink, drawn round the cap the keys or a press move, at one ring's offset, never as a box round the whole control (R-005, D-009).

aria-disabled=true.why: A scrubber with nothing loaded loses the cap's height and fades to half, and it cannot be moved.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion a seek lands at once with no travel and the index ink changes with no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the cap turns matte with a real border, the played stretch becomes Highlight, and the index, groove, buffer and chapter marks use system colours.

data-tint=warm.why: A warm source, such as a fireplace recording or a sunrise light scene, takes the warm amber glass range for its cap and played light.

data-tint=cool.why: A cool source, such as a fan or a night scene, takes the cool steel glass range for its cap and played light.

@media prefers-reduced-transparency: red.why: When the reader asks for less transparency the cap and the played light turn matte in the same tint, so the position still reads at once.

border-color.why: The index ink step on hover comes in over 120ms and goes back over 240ms on the decelerating curve, fast in and slow out.
